items.title: The carrier network is the strategic asset, not the software
items.summary: Alpega connects shippers, carriers, and logistics providers across 80 countries through an open network of 80,000+ vetted carriers, with hundreds of thousands of freight and vehicle offers transacted daily across the Teleroute, Wtransnet, and Bursa Transport exchanges. Every product — TMS, execution, procurement — sells better because this liquidity sits behind it.
items.implication: Model network liquidity (offers, matches, active members) as a first-class outcome that every persona's jobs depend on; product decisions that grow or protect liquidity outrank single-product features.

items.title: API-first execution is the wedge into enterprise accounts
items.summary: Alpega relaunched its Connected product as Alpega Transport Execution in January 2026: modular, API-driven, connecting a shipper's existing TMS, ERP, and planning tools directly to the carrier network at thousands of loads per day, with transparent shipper-pays pricing. The pitch is explicitly 'keep your systems, wire them to the network'.
items.implication: Treat ERP/TMS connectivity and integration onboarding time as product KPIs, not implementation details — the execution wedge lands only if integration is fast and the network answers on the other side.

items.title: Analyst positioning buys the enterprise conversation; lifecycle attach wins it
items.summary: Alpega TMS is positioned as a Challenger in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Transportation Management Systems (16 vendors evaluated, published March 2026) — its 15th recognition in this research. Analyst standing gets the Transportation Director's attention, but account economics come from expanding a single entry product into the full Plan-to-Settle lifecycle.
items.implication: Model per-account module attach and net revenue retention as the business KPIs behind enterprise personas; the strategy horizons should sequence entry product first, lifecycle attach second.

items.title: Trust is being productized as the exchange's core differentiator
items.summary: In February 2026 Alpega announced trust indicators evaluating network participants on compliance records, settlement behavior, and historical performance, positioning trust as what enables faster tendering, fewer exceptions, and dependable outcomes on the exchanges.
items.implication: Carrier vetting, trust scores, and payment security are revenue-bearing product surfaces, not back-office hygiene — wire them into every booking flow and monetize them as guarantees and trust reports.

items.title: A fifth of European truck kilometers are driven empty
items.summary: Eurostat reports that 21.6% of road freight vehicle-kilometers in the EU were driven empty in 2024 — 25.9% in national transport and 13.1% in international transport. Empty running is the structural inefficiency freight exchanges exist to attack, and it is largest exactly where small carriers operate.
items.implication: Empty-kilometer reduction is the quantifiable customer value of matching: build return-load matching, capacity publishing, and tour proposals around it, and measure personas on loaded-kilometer outcomes.

items.title: The driver shortage makes wasted truck hours the scarcest resource
items.summary: IRU's 2025 survey counts around 502,000 unfilled truck driver positions in Europe (a 13% shortage rate), with roughly 660,500 drivers expected to retire by 2030 and small operators hit hardest. Every hour a scarce driver spends waiting at a dock or searching for a load is capacity Europe cannot replace.
items.implication: Position dock scheduling, fast matching, and no-touch execution as driver-hour savers; shipper-side capacity coverage KPIs must assume structurally tight supply, not cyclical relief.

items.title: Cargo crime and phantom carriers are escalating into a strategic risk
items.summary: TAPA EMEA and IUMI warn of escalating cargo theft and freight fraud in Europe; across major European markets TAPA recorded 30,543 incidents in 2024-2025 with over 860 million euros in documented losses, and organized groups increasingly use identity fraud and fake carrier companies rather than physical theft alone.
items.implication: Fraud screening must sit at network signup, at booking, and in continuous monitoring — a single high-profile fraud incident can destroy exchange trust that took years to build; guarantee products price this risk.

items.title: Contract and spot rates are diverging — managing the mix is a product job
items.summary: The IRU/Ti/Upply benchmark shows European contract rates climbing to 136.9 in Q4 2025 (up 3.1 points year on year) while spot rates held at 135.1 (down 3.3 year on year) — contract and spot markets moving apart after converging mid-year. Shippers with the wrong contract-spot mix bleed money in both directions.
items.implication: Procurement, benchmarking, and spot cover must work as one loop: benchmark-informed tendering, measured spot exposure, and eventually automated spot-contract balancing per lane (the year-5 horizon).

items.title: CSRD turns shipment-level emissions data into a purchasing criterion
items.summary: The EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive requires large companies to report sustainability information including value-chain (scope 3) emissions under the European Sustainability Reporting Standards — pushing shippers to demand auditable, shipment-level transport emissions instead of spend-based estimates from their logistics platforms and carriers.
items.implication: Emissions reporting computed from execution records is a monetizable data product and a procurement differentiator; carrier emissions data quality becomes part of vetting and tender scoring.

items.title: A 440-billion-euro market of very small operators demands two-sided simplicity
items.summary: Ti sizes European road freight at about 440 billion euros in 2025, while IRU notes operators with fewer than ten employees account for 98% of EU road freight enterprises and 79% of the workforce. The demand side is concentrated enterprise; the supply side is radically fragmented small business.
items.implication: The platform must serve both extremes at once: deep enterprise integration for shippers, and mobile-first, low-friction, multi-language workflows for carriers — pricing and UX cannot be one-size-fits-all.

items.title: SaaS plus marketplace is a flywheel: shipper freight attracts carrier capacity
items.summary: Alpega's model combines enterprise SaaS (TMS, procurement, execution) with the freight-exchange network: more shipper freight flowing digitally attracts more carrier capacity, which improves coverage and price discovery for shippers, whose transactions feed data products (benchmarks, ETAs, trust scores) that deepen the moat. Reference shippers include Heineken, Asahi UK, Höganäs, and Barry Callebaut.
items.implication: Cross-side effects belong in the KPI model: shipper-side execution volume drives carrier-side contract connections and vice versa; strategy horizons for every persona should compound the flywheel, not optimize one side in isolation.

items.title: Payment security is the adoption lever for the long tail of carriers
items.summary: With cargo fraud escalating and small carriers operating on thin cash buffers, payment behavior and settlement security decide whether the long tail participates: TAPA EMEA highlights fraud targeting the transaction layer itself, and Alpega's trust indicators explicitly score settlement behavior alongside compliance.
items.implication: Payment guarantees, evidence-grade eCMR, and collections with network consequences are retention products for carriers and liquidity insurance for the whole exchange — model them with adoption and claims-ratio KPIs.
